He was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] at [[Little Elm High School]] in Little Elm, Texas. He was drafted by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] as the 24th overall pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Since his freshman season, Hampton played [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball for [[Little Elm High School]] in [[Little Elm, Texas]]. In his first high school game on November 17, 2016, he led all scorers with 33 points in a 78–52 win over [[Naaman Forest High School]].{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Bryan |title=Time for hoops: Little Elm dismantles Naaman in season opener |url=https://starlocalmedia.com/friscoenterprise/sports/time-for-hoops-little-elm-dismantles-naaman-in-season-opener/article_549fe754-acef-11e6-9276-1f3615fd89f0.html |website=Frisco Enterprise |publisher=Star Local Media |access-date=May 28, 2019 |date=November 17, 2016}} As a freshman, Hampton averaged 23.6 points, 7.2 rebounds, 4.2 assists, and 3.5 steals per game, leading Little Elm to a 29–5 record and the District 14-5A title.{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Bryan |title=Home is where the heart is: Little Elm basketball star R.J. Hampton decides to stay with Lobos |url=https://starlocalmedia.com/friscoenterprise/sports/home-is-where-the-heart-is-little-elm-basketball-star/article_39d93da4-7bd3-11e7-90ec-dbcdaa01e2f8.html |website=Frisco Enterprise |publisher=Star Local Media |access-date=May 28, 2019 |date=August 7, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Wixon |first1=Matt |title=SportsDayHS 2017 All-Area boys basketball teams, newcomer and coach of the year |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2017/03/23/sportsdayhs-2017-area-boys-basketball-teams-newcomer-coach-year |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=May 28, 2019 |date=March 23, 2017}} He was named to the [[MaxPreps]] Freshman All-American first team and earned Texas Association of Basketball Coaches (TABC) Class 5A All-State and ''[[The Dallas Morning News|Dallas Morning News]]'' All-Area Newcomer of the Year honors.{{cite web |title=2016-17 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Freshman All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/EVB78NqOWEaYDifF0xyXpg/2016-17-maxpreps-boys-basketball-freshman-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=May 28, 2019 |date=April 18, 2017}} In May 2017, Hampton announced that he was transferring to the nationally ranked basketball program of [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]], before deciding to return to Little Elm.{{cite web |last1=Wixon |first1=Matt |title=R.J. Hampton, one of the nation's top basketball recruits, ditches Montverde Academy to stay at Little Elm |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2017/08/04/star-guard-rj-hampton-one-nations-top-recruits-staying-little-elm-instead-transferring-montverde-academy |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=May 28, 2019 |date=August 4, 2017}} In the 2017–18 season, Hampton averaged 30.3 points, 8.8 rebounds, six assists, 4.4 steals, and 2.5 blocks per game, guiding Little Elm to a 28–8 record.{{cite web |last1=Florek |first1=Michael |title=Meet the best boys basketball players in Dallas: The 2018 Dallas Morning News all-area team |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2018/03/22/meet-best-boysbasketball-players-dallas-2018-dallas-morning-news-area-team |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=May 28, 2019 |date=March 22, 2018}} He garnered MaxPreps Sophomore All-American first team, ''[[USA Today]]'' All-Texas first team, and TABC 5A All-State recognition.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=2017-18 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/yL1wLxRGiUeRCLlOOrsePA/2017-18-maxpreps-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=May 28, 2019 |date=April 17, 2018}}{{cite web |title=2017-18 ALL-USA Texas Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/2017-18-all-usa-texas-boys-basketball-team |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=May 28, 2019 |date=April 16, 2018}} On December 14, 2018, Hampton scored 33 points in an 80–66 victory over [[South Garland High School]], matching up against fellow coveted recruit [[Tyrese Maxey]].{{cite web |last1=Jennings |first1=Randy |title=R.J. Hampton, Little Elm top Tyrese Maxey, South Garland in showdown of Texas' top basketball prospects |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2018/12/14/rj-hampton-little-elm-top-tyrese-maxey-south-garland-showdown-texas-top-basketball-prospects |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=May 29, 2019 |date=December 14, 2018}} On December 29, he posted a career-high 50 points, 12 rebounds, seven assists, and six steals in an 86–62 win over [[Coppell High School]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=Chosen 25 PG R.J. Hampton scores career-high 50 points |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/chosen-25-pg-r-j-hampton-scores-career-high-50-points |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=May 29, 2019 |date=December 29, 2018}} In February 2019, Hampton had another 50-point game in an 83–80 loss to [[Northwest High School (Texas)|Northwest High School]].{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Bryan |title=Column: Hampton robbed of District MVP |url=https://starlocalmedia.com/friscoenterprise/sports/column-hampton-robbed-of-district-mvp/article_0cbaa4ec-41c6-11e9-bbe4-573fb4339118.html |website=Frisco Enterprise |publisher=Star Local Media |access-date=May 29, 2019 |date=March 8, 2019}} As a junior, Hampton averaged 32 points, 9.7 rebounds, 6.4 assists, and 3.9 steals per game, helping Little Elm achieve a 24–10 record.{{cite web |title=R.J. Hampton 2018 - 2019 Texas Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/rj-hampton/37167 |publisher=[[Gatorade]] |access-date=May 29, 2019 |archive-date=October 21, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021051356/https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/rj-hampton/37167 |url-status=dead }} On March 15, he was named Texas [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]], becoming the first non-senior to win the award since [[Justise Winslow]] in 2013.{{cite web |last1=Hoyt |first1=Joseph |title=Little Elm star R.J. Hampton named Gatorade's Texas basketball Player of the Year and finalist for national award |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2019/03/15/little-elm-star-rj-hampton-named-gatorades-texas-basketball-player-year-finalist-national-award |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=April 30, 2019 |date=March 15, 2019}} He also earned ''USA Today'' All-USA first team and MaxPreps All-American second team distinction.{{cite web |title=2018-19 ALL-USA High School Boys Basketball: First Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/2018-19-all-usa-high-school-boys-basketball-first-team#slideIdslide-2 |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=April 30, 2019 |date=April 2, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=MaxPreps 2018-19 High School Boys Basketball All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/mdbwDYCSa02E7-TpRc5Gmg/maxpreps-2018-19-high-school-boys-basketball-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=April 30, 2019 |date=April 11, 2019}} On April 30, Hampton [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the 2019 class, forgoing his senior year and graduating from high school after about three weeks of online classes.{{cite web |last1=Hill |first1=Drew |title=Five-star Memphis basketball target R.J. Hampton reclassifies to 2019 |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2019/04/30/memphis-basketball-tigers-target-r-j-hampton-reclassifies-2019/3628389002 |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=April 30, 2019 |date=April 30, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Hampton was a consensus five-star recruit and ranked among the top six players in the 2019 recruiting class.{{cite web |title=R.J. Hampton, 2019 Point guard |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2019/r-j-hampton-182969 |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=May 29, 2019}}{{cite web |title=RJ Hampton, Little Elm, Combo Guard |url=https://247sports.com/Player/RJ-Hampton-46036336 |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=May 29, 2019}}{{cite web |title=R.J. Hampton |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/230214/rj-hampton |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=February 26, 2023}} On September 5, 2017, Christian Dawkins, an agent later indicted in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal|NCAA basketball corruption scandal]], expressed a desire to pay Hampton in emails sent to business partners. When the emails surfaced in 2019, Hampton's father denied ever meeting Dawkins.{{cite web |last1=Schlabach |first1=Mark |title=Christian Dawkins' emails detail payment plans to several players |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25210341 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=February 26, 2023 |date=January 3, 2019}} Before reclassifying on April 30, 2019, Hampton had been considered one of the best prospects in the 2020 class.{{cite web |last1=Newman |first1=Logan |title=Report: R.J. Hampton cuts list to four schools, could reclassify to 2019 |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/rj-hampton-top-four-duke-kansas-kentucky-memphis-report |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=May 29, 2019 |date=April 7, 2019}} He narrowed down his potential college destinations to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], and [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]].{{cite web |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Five-star guard RJ Hampton to play in Australian NBL, rejects Kansas, Memphis, Texas Tech |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/college-basketball-recruiting-five-star-guard-rj-hampton-to-play-in-australian-nbl-rejects-kansas-memphis-texas-tech |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=May 29, 2019 |date=May 28, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = R. J. Hampton | position = [[Point guard|PG]] | hometown = [[Little Elm, Texas|Little Elm, TX]] | highschool = [[Little Elm High School|Little Elm]] (TX) | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 180 | 40 = | commitdate = — | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 96 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = | scout ref title = | espn ref title = | rivals school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = | 247 overall = 5 | rivals overall = 6 | espn overall = 5 | accessdate = April 30, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==Professional career== ===New Zealand Breakers (2019–2020)=== On May 28, 2019, Hampton signed a multi-year deal with the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL), which is based in Australia, with the option to leave for the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).{{cite web |last1=Slagter |first1=Josh |title=RJ Hampton, a top-5 national recruit, chooses to play pro basketball in New Zealand: 'You can always go back to college' |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-rj-hampton-new-zealand-pro-basketball-college-20190528-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=May 29, 2019 |date=May 28, 2019}} He said that he skipped college basketball because he wanted to "live like a pro and to play with grown men and not have to juggle books and basketball."{{cite news |title=Top US prospect R.J. Hampton signs with New Zealand team |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/nba/top-us-prospect-rj-hampton-signs-with-new-zealand-team/2019/05/29/503db8f4-81d0-11e9-b585-e36b16a531aa_story.html |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=May 29, 2019 |date=May 29, 2019}} Hampton joined the Breakers through the NBL Next Stars program, which aims to develop [[NBA draft]] prospects.{{cite web |title=US Teen Sensation Signs with NZ Breakers |url=https://www.nzbreakers.basketball/news/article/us-teen-sensation-signs-with-nz-breakers |publisher=[[New Zealand Breakers]] |access-date=May 29, 2019 |date=May 28, 2019}}{{cite web |title=NBL to Fast Track Next Stars of the NBA |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/nbl-to-fast-track-next-stars-of-the-nba |publisher=[[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] |access-date=May 29, 2019 |date=March 2, 2018}} On September 20, he made his professional debut in a win over [[Melbourne United]], recording 11 points, three rebounds and four assists in 21 minutes.{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=R.J. Hampton drops 11 points in NBL debut with the NZ Breakers |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2019/09/20/r-j-hampton-nbl-new-zealand-breakers-debut-preseason-stats-highlights |website=The Rookie Wire |access-date=December 20, 2019 |date=September 20, 2019}} Two days later, he posted a season-high 20 points, five rebounds and three steals in a loss to the [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]].{{cite web |title=RJ Hampton shines, top scores as Breakers fall in second pre-season clash |url=https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/sport/basketball/rj-hampton-shines-top-scores-breakers-fall-in-second-pre-season-clash |website=[[TVNZ]] |access-date=January 18, 2020 |date=September 21, 2019}} On November 9, Hampton was ejected four minutes into a game against South East Melbourne after attempting to put his arm around the neck of opposing guard [[John Roberson]] during a scuffle.{{cite web |last1=Robinson |first1=Jesse |title=RJ Hampton ejected early in NBL tussle |url=https://www.espn.com/nbl/story/_/id/28039053 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=December 20, 2019 |date=November 9, 2019}} On December 11, it was announced that he would miss about four weeks of action with a hip injury.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Projected NBA lottery pick RJ Hampton to miss 4 weeks with hip injury |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28278222/|publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=December 20, 2019 |date=December 11, 2019}} On January 5, 2020, Hampton returned, scoring 11 points in a win over South East Melbourne.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28415031/|title=Sources: Hampton cleared; LaMelo remains out|date=January 3, 2020|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=January 3, 2020}} He parted ways with the Breakers on February 4 to return to the United States and prepare for the [[2020 NBA draft]]. Through 15 NBL games, Hampton averaged 8.8 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game, shooting 40.7 percent from the field.{{cite web |last1=Reive |first1=Christopher |title=RJ Hampton leaves New Zealand Breakers to prepare for NBA draft |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=12305812 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=February 3, 2020 |date=February 3, 2020}} Hampton was projected as a top 5 pick for the 2020 NBA draft heading into the season. ===Denver Nuggets (2020–2021)=== Hampton was drafted by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] as the 24th pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]], but his draft rights were later traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in a four-team trade involving the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] and [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on November 24, 2020.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-pick-zeke-rj-202011|title=Denver Nuggets select Zeke Nnaji, trade for R.J. Hampton in 2020 NBA Draft|work=NBA.com|date=November 24, 2020}} On December 1, 2020, the Denver Nuggets announced that they had signed Hampton.{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets sign Zeke Nnaji, R.J. Hampton to rookie contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-zeke-rj-20201201|date=December 1, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 1, 2020}} He played 25 games for the Nuggets, averaging 2.6 points and 2.0 rebounds in 9.3 minutes per game.{{Cite web|title=Magic Acquire R.J. Hampton, Gary Harris and First Round Draft Pick From Nuggets|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-acquire-rj-hampton-garry-harris-draft-pick-denver-nuggets-aaron-gordon-gary-clark-trade-20210325|access-date=April 9, 2021|website=Orlando Magic|language=en}} ===Orlando Magic (2021–2023)=== On March 25, 2021, Hampton, [[Gary Harris]], and a future first round pick were traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] in exchange for [[Aaron Gordon]] and [[Gary Clark (basketball)|Gary Clark]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-acquire-rj-hampton-garry-harris-draft-pick-denver-nuggets-aaron-gordon-gary-clark-trade-20210325|title=Magic Acquire R.J. Hampton, Gary Harris and First Round Draft Pick From Nuggets|work=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2021}} On April 4, Hampton was named in the starting lineup for the first time in his career against Denver Nuggets. He recorded 16 points, four rebounds, and three assists in 33 minutes.{{Cite web|title=Magic's R.J. Hampton: Drops 16 points in first start|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/magics-r-j-hampton-drops-16-points-in-first-start/|access-date=April 9, 2021|website=CBSSports.com|date=April 5, 2021 |language=en}} On May 17, he was named Eastern Conference rookie of the month for the month of May.{{Cite web|title=R.J. Hampton Named NBA Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-rj-hampton-named-nba-eastern-conference-rookie-of-the-month-20210517|access-date=May 18, 2021|website=Orlando Magic|language=en}} On December 29, 2022, Hampton was suspended by the NBA for one game without pay due to coming off the bench during an altercation in a game against the [[Detroit Pistons]] the day before.{{cite web |title=NBA announces suspensions from Pistons-Magic game |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-announces-pistons-magic-suspensions |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 31, 2022 |date=December 29, 2022}} On February 21, 2023, Hampton was waived by the Magic.{{Cite web |title=Orlando Magic PR on Twitter: "PRESS RELEASE: @OrlandoMagic waive R.J. Hampton" |url=https://twitter.com/Magic_PR/status/1628124976116076552 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=Twitter}} ===Detroit Pistons (2023)=== On February 23, 2023, Hampton signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{Cite web |title=Sean Corp on Twitter: "Detroit Pistons make RJ Hampton signing official shortly after game with Magic. Hampton, who was waived by Orlando, was in attendance at tonight's game." |url=https://twitter.com/sean_corp/status/1628954416718966786 |access-date=February 23, 2023 |website=Twitter}} He was waived by the Pistons on June 24.{{Cite web |date=June 24, 2023 |title=The Detroit Pistons announced today that the team has waived guard R.J. Hampton. |url=https://twitter.com/Pistons_PR/status/1672717526885715975 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=Twitter |language=en}} ===Miami Heat (2023–2024)=== On September 27, 2023, Hampton signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|title=HEAT Make Roster Moves|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-make-roster-moves-20230927|website=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2023|access-date=September 27, 2023}} He was waived on February 9, 2024.{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN ALONDES WILLIAMS TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-alondes-williams-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2024|access-date=February 10, 2024}} ===Capital City Go-Go (2024)=== On February 14, 2024, Hampton was acquired by the [[Capital City Go-Go]] after a trade with the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]]{{cite web|title=Capital City Go-Go Acquire R.J. Hampton via Trade with Sioux Falls Skyhawks|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/capital-city-go-go-acquire-r-j-hampton-via-trade-with-sioux-falls-skyhawks|website=NBA.com|date=February 14, 2024|access-date=February 15, 2024}} and on March 3, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Washington Wizards]], but didn't play for the team.{{cite web|title=Wizards Sign Champagnie to Two-Way Contract/Sign Hampton to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-champagnie-to-two-way-contract-sign-hampton-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 3, 2024|access-date=March 3, 2024}} On March 13, he rejoined Capital City.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Capital City Go-Go Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Capital-City-Go-Go/55/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 14, 2024}} ===Changsha Yongsheng (2025–2026)=== On November 14, 2025, Hampton signed with the [[Changsha Yongsheng]] of the [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]] in China.{{cite web |title=2020年24号秀！长沙勇胜官宣前NBA后卫RJ·汉普顿加盟 |url=https://news.zhibo8.com/nba/2025-11-14/6916ac3d074c1native.htm |website=直播吧 |access-date=November 14, 2025 |date=November 14, 2025}} ==National team career== Hampton won the gold medal at the [[2017 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] with the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States national under-16 team]]. In five games, he averaged nine points, 3.2 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=R.J. Hampton looking to win second straight gold medal with USA Basketball, plans to cut college list during winter |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2018/06/21/rj-hampton-looking-to-win-second-straight-gold-medal-with-usa-basketball-plans-to-cut-college-list-during-winter |publisher=ZagsBlog |access-date=April 30, 2019 |date=June 21, 2018}} He won another gold medal with the national under-17 team at the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]] but was limited to two games by a foot injury. Hampton averaged 7.5 points, 2.5 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game.{{cite web |last1=Riddle |first1=Greg |title=Denton Guyer's De'Vion Harmon and Little Elm's R.J. Hampton help USA win FIBA under-17 World Cup in Argentina
